member.summary: An angle, stored in degrees. It has no sign convention of its own. The domain's SignConvention covers that. member.name: T:geoDC.Measurements.CrsReference
member.summary: What a set of coordinates says about its coordinate reference system. A Defined reference points at a catalogue definition by its identifier (EPSG:4326, or a user definition's own id) and holds the coordinate epoch that dynamic frames need. member.name: T:geoDC.Measurements.GeodeticCoordinate
member.summary:
One position in a geodetic coordinate reference system: easting/northing (metres) on a projected grid or latitude/longitude (degrees) on an ellipsoid, each with an optional height in metres, or earth-centred X/Y/Z (metres). says which. The CRS itself is stored beside the value on the owning record, so this type does not depend on any catalogue. Unlike , which is a point in metres in the vessel frame, the ordinates here have geodetic meaning and are validated for it.
Formats through with the grammar in two segments, <horizontal>[;<height>]. A projected coordinate takes the units (m, cm, mm) and writes the unit once: $"{p:m3}" → 593000.000, 5750000.000, 12.500 m. A geographic coordinate takes deg (signed decimal degrees), dm (degrees and decimal minutes with a hemisphere letter) or dms (degrees, minutes and decimal seconds with a hemisphere letter): $"{p:dms2;m3}" → 51° 54' 00.00" N, 4° 06' 00.00" E, 50.000 m. A geocentric coordinate formats like a projected one with all three ordinates. When the height segment is omitted a projected coordinate reuses the horizontal format and a geographic one writes metres at full precision. The u flag drops the unit symbols; hemisphere letters stay because they carry the sign. The general format (null, empty or G) is full precision in metres or decimal degrees. Components are separated by the format provider's list separator, so a comma-decimal culture does not read ambiguously.

member.name: T:geoDC.Measurements.IsoTimestamp
member.summary: The ISO 8601 timestamp grammar shared by the date inputs, the time-bound filters and the timestamp columns, read and written with the invariant culture so a day and a month are never swapped by regional settings. Entry is lenient: a T or a space between date and time, a single-digit month, day or hour, omitted seconds, up to seven fractional digits, and a trailing Z, UTC or ±HH:mm offset. Minutes and seconds are always two digits: a trailing single digit is a field still being typed, and reading 00:0 as 00:00 would silently change what the operator meant. Text with a zone is converted to UTC and returned as . Text without one is returned as for the caller to interpret. Output is always the canonical form of a .

member.name: T:geoDC.Measurements.QuantityFormat
member.summary: The unit-and-precision format grammar shared by the measurement primitives: [+]<unit>[digits][t][u]. + signs non-negative values too, unit is one of the type's unit tokens, digits fixes the decimal places (omitted = full precision), t trims trailing zeros so digits becomes a maximum, and u drops the unit suffix. The trailing flags may come in either order. For example mm1, +mm1, m4, m3u, m3t, +deg3.

member.name: T:geoDC.Measurements.Sexagesimal
member.summary: Writes a non-negative degree magnitude as degrees and decimal minutes (dm) or degrees, minutes and decimal seconds (dms). The format's digits apply to the last component, which is rounded before the larger ones are split off so 59.9999' carries into the next degree instead of printing 60'. Minutes and seconds are zero-padded to two integral digits. Sign and hemisphere are left to the caller.
